# Template: sampling_dist
The central limit theorem as two stacked panels: any population distribution on top (skewed, uniform, bimodal or normal), and below it the distribution of SAMPLE MEANS for samples of size n — always bell-shaped, always centered on the population mean, and narrower by the square root of n. The sample size n is numeric, so `animate` can slide it and honestly squeeze the sampling distribution. Choose this scene for ANY request about the central limit theorem, sampling distributions, the distribution of sample means or averages, standard errors shrinking with sample size, or why averages are normal even when the data is not.
Parameter schema:
{
 "type": "object",
 "properties": {
  "shape": {
   "type": "string",
   "enum": [
    "skewed",
    "uniform",
    "bimodal",
    "normal"
   ],
   "description": "The population's shape (default skewed — the most instructive case)."
  },
  "n": {
   "type": "number",
   "minimum": 1,
   "maximum": 100,
   "multipleOf": 1,
   "description": "Sample size behind each mean, 1-100 (default 5). Numeric — animate it to watch the squeeze."
  },
  "show_normal": {
   "type": "boolean",
   "description": "Dashed normal overlay on the sampling distribution (default false)."
  },
  "title": {
   "type": "string"
  }
 }
}
Element ids your commands can reference:
- axes: both panels' axis lines and captions (a group)
- pop_curve: the population distribution (top panel)
- pop_mean: dashed line at the population mean (top)
- samp_curve: the distribution of sample means (bottom panel)
- samp_mean: dashed line at its center — the same mean
- n_label: the "means of samples of n = 5" caption
- se_bracket: a bracket at the sampling distribution's mean +/- one standard error — it narrows as n grows
- se_label: the bracket's width as a number ("± 0.63") — recomputed live while n animates
- normal_overlay: dashed normal on the sampling panel (when show_normal)
- title: figure title, when set
Examples:
Request: "Show the central limit theorem: a skewed population but normal sample means." → params: {"title":"The central limit theorem"}
Request: "What happens to the distribution of averages when the sample grows?" → params: {"shape":"bimodal","n":25,"title":"Averages of a two-humped world"}

In YAML: `template: sampling_dist` and `params:` per the schema above; commands name the element ids above.
